$comment: How V-ENT's frontend meets owner rules R55 to R61 (17 September 2026). Read by ~/.claude/skills/security-rules/scripts/check-security.mjs. The mapping table is 'Owner rules 55 to 61 in V-ENT' in ../CLAUDE.md. This app holds no database and no paid SDK: every record lives behind the Django API (../V-ENT-BACKEND), whose own security-rules.json and security/idor-cases.json carry R57 to R60 for the platform. The four API routes here are listed below with what each one is.

ownership.$comment: This app owns no records; its one server handler forwards a sign-in. The ownership cases are the platform's, kept and run against the Django API in the backend repo.

billing.na: no paid service is called from this app; Paystack is reached from the backend, and the site is served from the InterServer VPS whose register is ../V-ENT-BACKEND/security/billing-caps.md

allow.reason: NextAuth's own handler; it reads no record by id, it forwards a credential or a Google id_token to the backend's /auth/login/ and /auth/social-auth/, which decide
clears this browser's own session cookie; no record, no id
answers which build this instance serves; no record, no id
a link-preview image proxy restricted to the configured media host and path (allowedOrigins()); it serves public banners only and cannot be pointed anywhere else

the one input, src, is parsed with new URL() inside a try, then allowed only when its origin is in allowedOrigins() and its path starts /media/ or /static/; the upstream answer is refused unless its type is one of four image types and it is under 6 MB, and it is re-encoded before it is sent. Anything else is the fallback card

NextAuth's own handler: sign-in is decided by the backend (/auth/login/, /auth/social-auth/ verifying the Google id_token), which also refuses and rate limits; the handler writes only this browser's session cookie
clears this browser's own session cookie and nothing else; there is no account to check it against, and doing it for a signed-out browser is harmless

a failed credentials sign-in is logged in lib/authOptions.js authorize (vent.security, reason refused or backend_unreachable), and the backend logs the same refusal with the address; nothing typed is in either line
clearing a cookie is not a sign-in and cannot fail as one; there is nothing to log

extract-zip has no patched release (advisory says patched in <0.0.0). It reaches this repo only as a devDependency, puppeteer-core > @puppeteer/browsers, whose job is downloading a browser; the walk scripts point executablePath at the installed Chrome and never call it, and nothing ships it to production (the standalone build has no puppeteer). Read by hand 30 Sept 2026; revisit when puppeteer drops it
